notes:
Account summary: Trillium is a mid-sized healthcare payments processor (claims settlement + patient payments). Team runs PCI card processing and stores limited PHI for claims tying. Use case: low-latency fraud scoring + embeddings for reconciliation + conversational payments support.

Key players: CTO - Martina Cole (technical sign-off), Head of Risk - Derek Shaw (security gating), VP Product - Anisha Rao (use-case owner), Procurement lead - Mark Li. AE Jordan Meyers; SE Priya Khatri; CSM Luis Ortega engaged for POC.

What we pitched: Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem option) with customer-managed KMS, audit logging, and Optimize recommendations to reduce token spend for reconciliation flows. Proposed dedicated GPU pool for 99th %-tile latency SLA.

Security/legal thread: returned security questionnaire 2026-01-12 flagged two hard stops: (1) PCI scope cannot include third-party inference unless we provide validated SAQ A-EP or equivalent; (2) HIPAA requirement to prevent egress of PHI to any third-party compute unless BAA and encryption at rest and in transit with customer KMS + HSM-backed key management. Legal requested continuous attestation and quarterly audit reports.

POC / commercial: Completed technical POC (fraud model latency/throughput) 2025-11-03 — passed perf targets (p50 60ms, p95 180ms for batch size 8). Pricing was within range for Dedicated. Procurement wanted a single-vendor solution that covered both PCI and HIPAA without heavy integration overhead.

Conversation highlights (crisp call notes):
- "We can't sign off on PCI in a multi-tenant cloud without a certified payment module and documented SAQ." — Head of Risk (D. Shaw)
- "If we have to build tokenization ourselves it's a non-starter; too many teams involved." — VP Product (Anisha)
- "Board paused new platform spends for H1 FY26 due to macro headwinds." — Procurement (Mark Li)

Why stalled / lost: Two simultaneous blockers: (A) Security/legal declined the dual-scope approach — they insisted on an on-prem or pre-certified payment provider for PCI to avoid extra audit burden; (B) Internal budget freeze removed momentum and there is no committed exec/champion to drive carve-outs. HealthCloud AI won shortlist by offering an integrated, PCI-certified payments module and existing FedRAMP-like attestation for their healthcare offering.

Open questions / follow-ups captured:
- Can Redwood produce a templated SAQ/attestation for the Private deployment that reduces Trillium's audit lift? (they asked for example paperwork)
- Is there a supported on-prem HSM + BAA path we can document in detail?

Disposition guidance: Close-won unlikely in near term; recommend capturing detailed engineering gap report for PCI attestation and library of artifacts for BAAs. Add to win/loss with emphasis on build vs. buy for PCI-certified modules.

Sales shorthand: "High technical fit, stuck on compliance + budget; lost to a vendor with pre-certified PCI offering."
